Definition: properly, to move in a circle, i.e. (specifically) to march in a sacred procession, to observe a festival; by implication, to be giddy
BiblicalUsage: Chagag means to keep a feast, to march in a sacred dance, to celebrate. Moses told Pharaoh to let the people go so they could hold a feast to the LORD in the wilderness, and the law commands the feast of tabernacles and the feast of weeks, seven days of rejoicing before the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the first thing God asked Pharaoh for was not wages or weapons but a feast. Freedom in the Bible starts with worship, and worship starts with letting go.
